blockers: /new-world is documentation, not an executable end-to-end orchestrator. It assigns research, synthesis, design, implementation, repair, browser QA, database updates, and commits to an interactive Claude session; loop.mjs only advances a review state machine after the producer manually invokes each command.

Browser and presentation QA are hard-coded for zoo, waste, and shop. A third world requires editing present-shots.mjs and creating a new world-specific gameplay QA script, contradicting autonomous third-world transferability.

Both completed worlds bypassed failed design reviews: CODEX_TIMEOUT or a final FAIL was recorded as done_with_note and superseded by a later implementation review. This violates the claimed fail-closed gate.
The claimed zero-human-intervention evidence is contradicted by recorded user calibration and by pipeline decisions explicitly ruled per user calibration.
high: The producer supplies the complete reviewer prompt file. The harness enforces output shape and score minima but does not construct or constrain review scope, trusted context, evidence inputs, or adversarial wording, so producer influence is structurally possible.

present-shots.mjs does not fail when correct-play bots fail, does not verify expected screens were reached, and does not capture or assert console/network errors, yet pipeline.json claims full flows and no console errors.

Presentation QA is a standalone command with no orchestration or completion-state integration. Nothing mechanically prevents pipeline.json or the overall factory from being marked complete without running it.

Art reuse is automatically recorded as qa_passed with inherited QA and no Series Style Gate. CSS/SVG work is recorded as an in-session task without an artifact hash or art QA, allowing unreviewed visuals around the advertised binding art gates.

Art QA and general Codex review/task transports do not strip API-key environment variables. Only art-provider applies SAFE_ENV, so the claimed mechanical subscription-only boundary is not uniformly enforced.

Observability is fragmented: codex-task writes routing-log.jsonl, loop reviews write per-run logs, while direct codex calls in art QA/provider are not routed through either logging mechanism. Delegations and visual reviews can occur with no central trace.

Pipeline metrics are manually asserted aggregates without schemas or derivation. Waste reports 10 delegations and zoo 9, while routing-log contains only one world research delegation for each and cannot substantiate those totals.

Waste and zoo pipeline records are internally inconsistent with completion claims: waste accepts a timed-out design confirmation; zoo accepts a final design FAIL48; zoo still has commit pending despite being presented as an end-to-end completed world.
medium: loop.mjs treats reviewer transport failure as HUMAN_REQUIRED and terminates permanently; this is fail-closed for quality but disproves zero-human completion during ordinary timeout or malformed-output failures.

The numeric two-axis completion threshold is 60 in codex-review.mjs, while the rubric calls 75+ a completion candidate. Threshold semantics are split between prose and code and permit mechanically valid PASS scores in the rubric's improvement range.
Art thresholds and category lists are duplicated in style-contract.md, new-world.md, and art-qa.mjs, creating drift risk.
The fixed art reference set silently drops missing files instead of requiring the declared set to be complete. Generation and QA may therefore run with fewer references than the contract claims.
Provider availability is trusted from a persistent provider-status.json probe; no freshness or expiry is enforced despite new-world.md requiring re-probing when status changes.

run IDs and generated art are nondeterministic, browser bots depend on timing and random game state, and pipeline.json records aggregate outcomes rather than seeds, prompts, artifact hashes, environment versions, or reproducibility inputs.
World-specific gameplay QA scripts mirror implementation rules and constants, increasing correlated-error risk and requiring bespoke human/agent authorship for every new world.
low: codex-review.mjs extracts a JSON object from surrounding free text despite documenting a strict single-object response, weakening transport strictness.
routing-log entries retain temporary absolute prompt paths that are non-portable and may disappear, reducing audit reproducibility.
pipeline.json status and metrics are unconstrained free-form strings such as done_with_note and mobile+desktop full flow rather than mechanically validated records.

recommended_actions: Implement a single executable new-world orchestrator that owns every phase, validates prerequisites and outputs, invokes repair loops, and derives pipeline state instead of allowing prose status edits.

Replace present-shots.mjs with registry-driven world traversal and declarative per-game adapters; fail if expected screens, failure/retry/success paths, console checks, or network checks are not observed.
Make design review binding: timeout, malformed output, or FAIL must prevent implementation/completion until a successful re-review passes; never substitute a later review of a different artifact.

Generate reviewer prompts inside the harness from immutable rubric templates and explicit artifact allowlists; hash and log the exact prompt, rubric, artifact set, reviewer output, and producer identity.
Route every Codex invocation through one transport that uniformly strips API credentials, verifies OAuth/subscription mode, enforces timeouts, and appends tamper-evident routing records.
Make Series Style and Presentation verdict artifacts mandatory dependencies of the completion state; apply real QA to reused and CSS/SVG assets or explicitly exclude them with validated criteria.
Derive metrics from event logs and artifact manifests; record seeds, commands, prompts, hashes, tool/model versions, timestamps, retries, and gate verdict paths.
Create a generic gameplay-QA contract with reusable adversarial strategies so a third world adds declarative cases rather than editing harness code.
Centralize all thresholds and required categories in one machine-readable policy consumed by docs, review transport, art QA, and completion validation.

Re-run a genuinely unseen third world from a clean checkout with no harness edits and no user interaction; treat any manual calibration, prompt repair, browser steering, or pipeline.json editing as an intervention.
